en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika), the Couplets on the Fetters (Saññojanaduka), etc.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is a fetter, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and is not a fetter, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are six; under object condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are six.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is a tie, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and is not a tie, by way of root condition … pe ….

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is an *ogha* (flood), there arises a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, but not an *ogha*, by way of root condition … [as above] … Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is a *yoga* (bond), there arises a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, but not a *yoga*, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are six under root; three under object … [as above] … six under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is an hindrance (*nīvaraṇa*), there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive, and which is not an hindrance, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are six;
under object-condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are three ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*) there are six.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is an adherence (*parāmāsa*), there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive, and which is not an adherence, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are six; in the object condition, three ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, six.
